governing_intent: Implement the deterministic, I/O-free Execution Coordination domain kernel that owns released-BIU admission, lifecycle policy, scheduling, custody gating, verdict admissibility, and the BIU contract model.
summary: PY-02 is bounded, coherent, and executable within approved authority. It implements pure policy only; persistence, adapters, runtime invocation, and operational integration remain assigned to later BIUs.
implementation_unknowns: Choose immutable Python value types, typed errors/results, canonical serialization, and a cryptographic digest algorithm.
Define pure-function APIs and table-driven fixtures for contract validation, admission, lifecycle transitions, scheduling, and verdict evaluation.
Represent trusted independent-read-back evidence as a domain input without performing retrieval in the pure domain.
Extend the existing AST fitness checker with a scoped detection set for direct clock, randomness, and identifier-generation imports.
verification_assessment: The contract requires real executable proof: deterministic unit and table-driven tests for every acceptance rule; fitness checks that fail on deliberate violating fixtures and pass on the actual tree while retaining real exit status; continued PY-01 fitness coverage; and a passing Node suite. The existing PY-01 fitness harness already demonstrates the required fixture-versus-tree pattern and is a suitable extension point.
material_risks: The precise canonical serialization and digest representation must be chosen deterministically; this is constrained implementation detail, not an owner decision.
Closure actions must remain contract-provided policy data; PY-02 must not pre-implement persistence, publication, worker invocation, or runtime custody mechanics assigned to later BIUs.

The inspected checkout is on main but has unrelated untracked files and is one commit ahead of origin/main; this does not alter contract readiness, but implementation must establish its authoritative baseline before editing.
next_action: Record READY, then advance PY-02 through the authorized TASKS-to-READY workflow; do not implement until separately authorized.
rationale: Founder-approved authority fixes the ownership boundary, lifecycle vocabulary, release ON/OFF policy, budget fail-closed behavior, concurrency direction, candidate-custody invariant, Python module boundary, and Node coexistence constraints. SWF-12 additionally resolves provider-neutral candidate custody. The pre-Python gate found zero unresolved Founder-level decisions, while remaining API, schema, and fitness-rule detail is normal engineering work. PY-02's scope, non-goals, requirement extents, dependency, and mechanical acceptance criteria align with the approved Wave 1 DAG without creating a second decision center.
